claim: The University of Iceland's application deadline page lists the autumn undergraduate deadline of 5 June under a heading for Icelandic and Nordic citizens, a group that includes every Nordic citizen (Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian or Swedish) applying from Denmark, but not other EU/EEA citizens.
excerpt: Icelandic and Nordic citizens — Undergraduate studies: 5 June
interpretation: Read literally, this makes 5 June the deadline for Nordic citizens (Danish, Finnish, Icelandic, Norwegian or Swedish), including those applying from Denmark. That reading is contradicted by the university's own FAQ, which is recorded separately as ev-hi-is-faq-5-june. This record deliberately does not resolve the two: the convenient reading here is the later deadline, and preferring it is exactly the choice that costs a student a year if it is wrong.

notes: Both this page and the FAQ were read on 2026-09-23 and both were live. The contradiction is the publisher's, not a stale copy on our side.

attestation.by: the deadline research pass, Nordic and Baltic group
attestation.note: Read against the source page on 2026-09-23, alongside the FAQ it contradicts.

claim: The University of Iceland's FAQ gives the same 5 June deadline to international students who have lived in Iceland and are living in Iceland, and does not mention Nordic citizens at all.
excerpt: International students who have lived in Iceland og are living in Iceland — 5 June
interpretation: Read literally, this excludes a Nordic citizen applying from Denmark who has not lived in Iceland. It cannot both be true and ev-hi-is-deadline-page-5-june be true, because the two describe different groups as the one 5 June belongs to. The untranslated Icelandic "og" left in the middle of an English sentence is worth recording: it is what a partial translation that has fallen out of step with the page it contradicts looks like from the outside, and it is a reason to suspect this page is the stale one — but a suspicion is not a fact, and the product declines to state a date on the strength of it.

notes: The resolution is not ours to make. admission@hi.is is the address that can settle it, and the country record tells the student to ask before relying on 5 June.

claim: Iceland has seven higher education institutions, four public (University of Iceland, University of Akureyri, Agricultural University of Iceland, Hólar University) and three private (Reykjavík University, Bifröst University, Iceland University of the Arts). There is no strict university versus applied split; the system combines comprehensive universities and specialised institutions.
excerpt: There are currently seven higher education institutions in Iceland … both comprehensive universities (e.g. University of Iceland) and specialized institutions (e.g. arts, agriculture, marine sciences).
interpretation: Eurydice is an EU information network, not the Icelandic rule-owner, so it is classed as reference material and used only for the descriptive sector picture. Its count of seven predates Hólar University joining the University of Iceland's university complex as Háskóli Íslands á Hólum (ev-is-holar-in-hi); the site now counts six.
